tasks.task: Map patient flow and write front desk procedures

items.when: When the path from booking to follow-up has pinch points and the desk needs written steps
Before writing, to draw the flow in lanes with times and find the stage holding things up
When the approved intake process exists and needs plain steps for front desk staff
When a procedure is drafted, to test it for gaps and make a short deck to teach it
When hand-offs between desk and clinician fail, to replace vague notes with clear observations

tasks.task: Find the desk's busiest minutes and what to change

items.when: When the waiting room backs up or calls ring out at the same times each day
When there are timings or logs, to map the delay and compare staff capacity options
When weighing a second person at the desk against staggered slots, to test each before trying it
When the wait cannot be cut, to change how it feels and what patients are told

tasks.task: Build the appointment book template

items.when: When each clinician and room needs slot types, lengths, buffers and emergency slots set out
When patients book online, to set open times, the questions asked and the prep messages
After a month on the new template, to see how much of each clinician's paid time was used

tasks.task: Build the staff rota with cover rules

items.when: When desk and support staff need a weekly rota that covers every open session
When the rota must follow the appointment book session by session
When cover must match the busy hours within each person's limits, with a cost check
When the team wants a fairer pattern, to try a rotation for late and weekend sessions
When only one person can do a task, to map who covers it and what each backup must learn
Each week, to spot sessions and tasks left without cover during leave

tasks.task: Design the recall and reactivation process

items.when: When patients fall off the books because nobody owns who is due, who calls and what happens next
When the recall steps need a flowchart, who does what and the edge cases
When recalls are logged as dated rows, to count those due, contacted and booked each month

tasks.task: Write recall and reminder messages

items.when: When the process is agreed and each step needs its message, by letter, text or email
When reminders go by text, to write the sequence with consent and opt-out wording
When a reminder reads cold or nagging, to try another tone with the facts unchanged
Before an email recall is scheduled, to tighten it and fix the subject line
Before messages go live, to check each interval, fee and time against what the clinicians set
When patients read the reminder and still do not book, to cut the effort the next step takes

tasks.task: Cut no-shows and late cancellations

items.when: When attendance records are to hand, to find which days, slots and patient groups miss most
When the cancellation and late arrival terms exist but patients do not understand them
After a change, to see whether no-show and late cancellation rates moved

tasks.task: Build the monthly practice KPI pack

items.when: When the practice system exports are in and the owner wants one page of numbers
Before building, to pick the few measures the desk team can move
When the owners and the desk need different views of the same numbers
When the exports are dated rows and you need monthly counts and rates you can trace
When the pack is needed every month and should be rerun, not rebuilt
Before the pack goes to the owners, to catch broken formulas and wrong totals

tasks.task: Run the monthly practice review

items.when: In the first week of each month, to review the numbers and agree a short list of fixes
After each review, to check last month's open actions and set the next agenda
When the same number slips for a third month, to find the cause and a way to prevent it

tasks.task: Set out fee information and estimates

items.when: When the practice needs a price list page, an estimate template and a rule for when estimates are due
When fees go up, to tell patients in a letter that keeps most of them
Before publishing, to check the page against approved service facts and flag unsupported lines
When the fee page is drafted, to read it as a patient and list what they would still have to ask

tasks.task: Set up the patient records request procedure

items.when: When requests for copies of records need a desk procedure and a log from the day they arrive
When a request has arrived, to list the steps to find the data and draft the reply
When the practice is in the US, to check the procedure for HIPAA gaps

tasks.task: Plan who can see and do what in the practice system

items.when: When each person, and any AI agent, should have the narrowest role that does the job
When staff share logins or passwords, to rank the gaps and write a one-page policy
Before an AI tool touches patient data, to check its terms on training and liability
When staff already use AI tools and there is no rule on what may go into them
When the desk handles email all day and needs one page of rules and a short drill

tasks.task: Respond to a patient data incident

items.when: When anyone suspects patient data went where it should not: wrong recipient, lost device, odd login
In the first hour, to set severity, who to tell and what to preserve
Before a letter goes to an affected patient, to check every promise in it can be kept
After the incident, to write a no-blame report and a safer desk procedure

tasks.task: Take over a practice in the first 30 days

items.when: When a new manager starts or an owner takes the desk back after a manager leaves
When the practice has old procedures, to find stale pages, missing owners and gaps
When nothing is written down, to decide what to write first and where it lives
When admin work is behind, to find the step that slows the queue

tasks.task: Reply to patient complaints and public reviews

items.when: When a complaint arrives, to read its tone, urgency and warning signs before replying
When the reply is about bills, appointments or insurance and needs privacy checks
When the first draft sounds defensive, to get a version that names the feeling
Before sending, to check each promise and flag tone
When public reviews come in, to draft replies and hold risky ones for the owner
When the reply follows policy but leaves the patient worse off

tasks.task: Keep referral paperwork moving

items.when: When referrals pass to another administrator, to list what was sent, received and booked
On a schedule, to find referrals with no confirmation and draft the follow-ups

tasks.task: Reconcile insurer payments and chase balances

items.when: When claims owed and insurer payments must be matched to the bank deposit, using totals only
When remittances, offsets and bank receipts do not agree, to reconcile them line by line
When patient balances are overdue, to write each reminder gentle or firm

tasks.task: Write new patient information and an intake form

items.when: When the desk answers the same questions daily, to turn them into one clear page
When the new patient form is long, to stage it so people finish it
When forms and letters use clinic words, to rewrite them in the words patients say
Before publishing, to check each line against facts the clinicians approved

tasks.task: Train front desk staff on the procedures

items.when: When the written procedures are the base for what new staff must learn
After a training session, to make a one-page handout staff can use at the desk
When a receptionist starts, to plan pre-start checks, the first week and 90-day goals
Each month, to flag procedures that no longer match how the desk works

tasks.task: Set stock levels for clinic supplies

items.when: When supplies run out or expire, to set par levels, expiry rules and an emergency stock
Each month, to review stock-outs and waste alongside the other numbers

tasks.task: Choose or switch the practice system

items.when: When practice systems are being compared, to score each against the practice's needs
When the switch is agreed, to plan notice dates and a staged move that drops no bookings
When patient and booking data must move, to map fields, checks and a way back

tasks.task: Price a practice membership plan

items.when: When the owners want a monthly plan, to set tier prices and flat fee or pay per use
When the plan could be one tier or several, to compare two shapes with the money shown
When the plan is priced, to make sure the fee page and estimates say the same thing

always.when: Before a procedure, letter or pack is shared, to catch typos and a service named two ways

helpers.when: When the job is phone scripts, greetings and day-to-day desk replies
When rotas raise contract, leave or working-time questions, or a hire is needed
When patient data rules, regulator reporting or inspection readiness need a regional check
When access roles, backups or device security must be set up, not only planned
When takings, insurer payments and the accounts need matching every month
When reviews are a serious problem or the practice wants a steady way to earn them

gaps: No library item builds an appointment book template by clinician and room with slot types, buffers and emergency slots
No library item designs a recall or reactivation process, or writes recall messages for patients or pet owners
No library item writes front desk phone scripts, greetings and call handling steps for a practice
No library item builds a staff rota that follows the appointment book with break and cover rules by region
No library item writes a fee estimate template or a rule for when a written estimate is due
No library item sets up a records request log with deadlines by region; the reply drafter covers one request
No library item plans role-based access inside a practice system, or reviews who has which role
No library item gives data incident steps and notification clocks for patient data by region
No library item defines practice measures such as chair-time use, recall rate and wait-list fills
No library item covers wait-list management or end-of-day desk cash-up
No library item offers clearly different versions of a reminder or recall message to compare
